name: Chang'e-7 (orbiter, lander, rover, hopper) — intended
summary: Illuminated rim of Shackleton (SE ridge/rim); note: unofficial

facts.label: Status
facts.value: PLANNED (2026 launch and Nov 2026 landing SUPERSEDED)

name: Shackleton crater
summary: Pole lies on its rim; PSR floor ~88-90 K; rim peaks sunlit ~80-90% of the time; >= 20 km3 impact melt; interior wall ~30 deg; rim blocks likely Shackleton ejecta that may expose SPA-related lithologies

facts.label: Size
facts.value: D 21.0 km, depth 4.2 km, floor 6.6 km

facts.label: Age
facts.value: Late Imbrian: rim 3.51 (+0.05/-0.08) Ga (Tye 2015); 3.60/3.69 Ga (Zuber 2012, flat floor/ejecta)

name: Shackleton-de Gerlache Connecting Ridge (junction with Shackleton rim)
summary: 1:8,000 geomorphic map (Icarus 2022, pii S0019103522000835); ~8 m blocks near junction are primary sampling targets; flat spot with line of sight into Shackleton PSR; illumination 92.27-95.65% at 2-10 m, longest darkness 3-5 days

facts.label: Age
facts.value: Ancient ridge mantled by Shackleton ejecta

name: de Gerlache crater
summary: PSR pocket incl. possible CO2 cold trap; 2022 study of 'slope exposed ice'

name: Haworth crater
summary: Large PSR; coldest areas never exceed ~40 K

name: Shoemaker crater
summary: H ~146 ppm (LP) / 220-245 ppm (LEND interp.); strongest, most uniform LAMP water-band signal of the four; possibly ~5%+ subsurface ice

facts.label: Size
facts.value: D 50.9 km (52 km in Tye), depth 3.81 km

name: Faustini crater
summary: 664 km2 PSR (3rd largest); floor may hold ejecta from Imbrium, Orientale, Schrodinger; radar-bright signal probably rocks (ShadowCam)

name: Nobile crater
summary: Former VIPER site on west rim (Mons Mouton side); Griffin Mission One to land near Nobile with Astrolab FLIP rover

name: Mons Mouton (formerly Leibnitz Beta)
summary: Near PSRs and extended illumination; IM-2 landed at -84.7906, 29.1958; IM-4 and Chang'e-8 planned for the plateau

name: Malapert Massif (Artemis region centre)

name: Cabeus crater
summary: LCROSS ground truth (5.6 +/- 2.9 wt% water + other volatiles); impact at -84.6796, -48.7093
limitations: Centre conflict: this note uses Wikipedia -84.9, -35.5; USGS Gazetteer list gives -85.33, -42.13 (see psr_and_ice.json).

name: Schrodinger basin (context, outside 80 S)
summary: Volcanic vent (Schrodinger G) and lava flows; target of the Farside Seismic Suite

name: Southernmost catalogued lunar pit: Schomberger A 1
summary: No listed pit lies poleward of 80 S (next are the Rutherfurd pits near -60.78); catalogue reported as 281 impact-melt, 15 mare, 5 highland pits. Natural-shelter credit should be zero poleward of 80 S (researcher inference).
evidence: ESTABLISHED for the catalogue; polar imaging hampered by lighting

name: Haworth (Tye et al. 2015)
evidence: MODEL age (Neukum chronology; LOLA 20 m DTM; 1-sigma counting errors only)
limitations: Pre-Nectarian absolute ages 'particularly uncertain' (no sample calibration beyond ~3.9 Ga). Coordinates from Wikipedia. Lemelin 2021 lists model age 4.18 Ga.
